input.quote: 10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns binding clause. It contains no assignment mechanics at all: it does not give us an express right to assign to an affiliate or to a transaction successor, imposes no consent gate (or reasonableness standard) on HDI's assignment, and leaves HDI free to assign the Agreement — including to a Deerskin competitor. It therefore fails the fallback (mutual successor assignment on written notice, with consent, not unreasonably withheld, for other assignments) on material terms. No change-of-control termination right exists elsewhere in the document (Section 4 termination and the Article 10 miscellaneous run are silent), but nothing confirms the position, so we have added it in the same insertion. We inserted one short paragraph after 10.3 rather than rewriting the existing sentence, which is preserved verbatim.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10.3 only binds successors and assigns; it gives us no express right to assign to an affiliate or transaction successor and leaves HDI free to assign to anyone, including a competitor. We have added our standard assignment terms, including confirmation that a change of control of the Company gives HDI no termination right.

ops.text: The Company may assign this Agreement, without HDI's consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets. HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, and may not in any event assign to a competitor of the Company. A change of control of the Company shall not give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement.

mappings.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
